shadows.name: ambient-float
shadows.purpose: Rare lift for transient floating elements.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus visibility on fields and actions.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Restrained state feedback; disabled under reduced motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single decisive action in a payment region.

components.name: Order Field
components.description: A labeled, high-contrast business data field.

components.name: Asset Toggle
components.description: A compact, explicitly selected SUI/USDC choice.
components.css: .ds-assets{display:inline-flex;padding:3px;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:9px;background:white}.ds-assets button{height:36px;padding:0 12px;border:0;border-radius:6px;background:transparent;color:var(--ink);font:700 .75rem/1 Inter,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-assets button[aria-checked=true]{background:var(--surface-strong)}.ds-assets button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:1px}

components.name: Payment Panel
components.description: The continuous settlement ledger, not a dashboard card.
components.css: .ds-payment{width:300px;padding:30px;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:14px;background:var(--surface);color:var(--ink);display:grid;gap:14px;font:400 .82rem/1.5 Inter,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-payment small{color:var(--primary);font-weight:700}.ds-payment strong{font-size:2rem}.ds-payment hr{width:100%;border:0;border-top:1px solid var(--border)}.ds-payment b{text-align:right}

components.name: Primary Navigation
components.description: Two durable destinations with a ruled active state.
components.css: .ds-nav{display:flex;height:56px;gap:6px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);background:white}.ds-nav button{position:relative;padding:0 12px;border:0;background:transparent;color:var(--ink-soft);font:700 .875rem/1 Inter,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-nav button.active{color:var(--ink)}.ds-nav button.active:after{content:'';position:absolute;right:10px;bottom:0;left:10px;height:2px;background:var(--primary)}.ds-nav button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:-2px}

components.name: Receipt Drop Zone
components.description: A clear local-file verification entry point.

narrative.overview: PayProof should feel like the cleanest page in a well-kept business ledger: quiet, exact, and composed when money changes hands. Strong type hierarchy and ruled structure carry the interface; color is used to establish action and status, never to manufacture excitement.
keyCharacteristics: Dense enough for work, spacious enough for review
Fluid from 320px mobile to wide desktop

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Marine cobalt is the only broad saturated surface. Status colors remain small and semantic.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from adjacent paper tones and one-pixel rules, not translucent overlays.

rules.name: The Numbers Stay Still Rule
rules.body: Amounts, addresses, hashes, and ledger values never use decorative italics or animated counters.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: If every section casts a shadow, the hierarchy has failed. Restore borders and tonal contrast instead.

dos: Do keep order entry and settlement visible in one continuous workflow.
Do use the 44px control minimum, visible focus, semantic labels, and live status announcements.
Do pair every color state with explicit language or an icon.
Do let long identifiers wrap safely and test at 320px width and 200% text size.
Do explain whether a transaction is unsigned, submitted, indexing, finalized, or failed.
donts: Don't introduce neon crypto dashboards, trading-terminal density, or speculative token imagery.
Don't copy generic corporate banking templates or scatter the workflow into dashboard card grids.
Don't use glass-heavy surfaces, glassmorphism, blurred panels, or translucent decoration.
Don't add anonymous “Web3” decoration or make users understand blockchain internals before paying.
Don't use gradients, gradient text, excessive pills, floating rounded rectangles, or bounce easing.
Don't publish private customer, line-item, or notes content on-chain; the public layer receives only its hash and essential payment facts.
